Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with wheeze and shortness of breath for 2–3 days
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Wheeze and SOB x2–3 days

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Initially reported fever but measured temperature was 37°C
Exertional dyspnea severe enough that patient cannot walk to work
Sometimes struggles to finish sentences due to shortness of breath
Climbing stairs is tolerated without significant symptoms
History of childhood asthma described as quite bad with inhaler use, occasional hospital visits, no ICU admissions, and missed school
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Childhood asthma “quite bad”; used inhalers; occasional hospital visits; no ICU; missed school

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Stopped regular asthma medications approximately 3–4 years ago
Currently uses salbutamol as needed every few weeks and before exercise
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: currently uses salbutamol PRN every few wks and before exercise

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Does not use a spacer with inhalers
Does not have a peak flow meter at home
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: no peak flow meter at home

Past_Medical_History.content: Childhood asthma requiring inhalers and occasional hospital visits but no ICU admissions and causing missed school
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Childhood asthma “quite bad”; used inhalers; occasional hospital visits; no ICU; missed school

Medications.content: No regular medications for hay fever

Usually walks to work but is currently working from home or on sick leave
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: usually walks to work, currently WFH/sick leave

Assessment.content: Asthma exacerbation with 2–3 days of wheeze and shortness of breath, cough without sputum, no hemoptysis or chest pain, exertional limitation, sometimes speech-limiting, and afebrile by measurement
Assessment.source_text: 1. Asthma exacerbation — 2–3 d wheeze/SOB with cough; no sputum/hemoptysis/CP; exertional limitation; sometimes speech-limiting; afebrile by measurement

Plan_of_Care.content: For asthma exacerbation, increase salbutamol to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially
Prescribe a spacer and have pharmacist demonstrate its use
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Rx spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate use

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe a peak flow meter and have patient record peak expiratory flow morning and evening for one week
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Rx peak flow meter; record PEF AM/PM x1 wk

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange a phone review with peak flow readings and consider need for additional inhaler
Plan_of_Care.source_text: phone review with readings; may need additional inhaler

Plan_of_Care.content: Safety-net advice: call if high temperature or worsening wheeze
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety-net: call if high temperature or worsening wheeze

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange review in approximately one week or earlier if symptoms worsen
Plan_of_Care.source_text: arrange review ~1 wk or earlier if worse

Plan_of_Care.content: For allergic rhinitis, start regular over-the-counter antihistamine
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Start regular OTC antihistamine (clinician to note specific option)

Follow_up_Information.content: Phone review planned after one week of peak flow recordings
